mainTopic: צדקה and the swindlers; whether a poor person must sell his belongings; how to set an orphan daughter's dowry
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of רבי חנינא and a 'poor' man who turned out to live in luxury. רבי חנינא responds with רבי אלעזר's teaching that we should be grateful to swindlers, since they give us some excuse for not helping every poor person. The גמרא adds that ignoring צדקה is like עבודה זרה, and that anyone who fakes need will end up truly needy. It then asks whether a poor person must sell his belongings before taking צדקה, and gives two different answers, from רב זביד and רבא בריה דרבה and from רב פפא. A new משנה teaches that an orphan girl given too small a dowry may claim the proper amount when she grows up. רבי יהודה and חכמים argue about how to measure that amount. The גמרא shows that שמואל, who estimates by the father, follows רבי יהודה, and that this is the הלכה. It then explains that when the father's intent cannot be assessed, the daughter gets רבי's fixed tenth, and it shows how that tenth is calculated so the son is not left with nothing.

steps.title: The overheard question: silver or gold tablecloths?
steps.stepSummary: This ends the story from the previous page: רבי חנינא's wife heard people asking the poor man whether he dines on silver or gold tablecloths.
steps.simpleTranslation: [They were asking him:] Do you eat on silver tablecloths or on gold tablecloths?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a story that began on the previous page. רבי חנינא's wife reports what she overheard, which shows that the 'poor man' was actually living in luxury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא used to send this man money every ערב שבת. His wife came back saying he doesn't need it, because people were asking him which fancy tablecloths he uses. This sets up רבי חנינא's reaction in the next step.

phrases.english: On silver tablecloths or on gold tablecloths?
phrases.notes: These are the words the wife overheard people asking the poor man. The story started on the previous page.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a story begun on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man receiving רבי חנינא's charity was living in luxury.

steps.title: Be grateful to the swindlers
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא responds with רבי אלעזר's teaching: we should thank the רמאין, because without them we would be sinning every day by not helping the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: This is what רבי אלעזר meant when he said: Come, let us be grateful to the swindlers. If not for them, we would be sinning every day, as the פסוק says: 'And he will cry out to ה׳ against you, and it will be a sin in you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא does not get angry about being fooled. Instead, he quotes רבי אלעזר, who says the fakers actually do us a favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that when a poor person cries out to ה׳ because we ignored him, we are guilty of a sin. Since there are fakers, we have some excuse for not giving to everyone who asks. That makes our failure to help the real poor less blameworthy.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us be grateful, show appreciation

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is NOT praising fraud. His point is that because fakers exist, we are not fully blamed for failing to help every person who asks.

phrases.english: He said: This is what Rabbi Elazar said:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי חנינא, the one who had been sending this man money.

phrases.english: Come and let us be grateful to the swindlers,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִלְמָלֵא הֵן, הָיִינוּ חוֹטְאִין בְּכׇל יוֹם,
phrases.english: for were it not for them, we would be sinning every day,
as it is said: "And he will cry out to ה׳ against you
and it will be a sin in you."
phrases.notes: דברים 15:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי חנינא's reaction to discovering the man was not needy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Swindlers give us some excuse for not helping every poor person, so we are not guilty of sinning every day.

steps.title: Ignoring צדקה is like idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה teaches that someone who looks away from giving צדקה is like one who serves עבודה זרה, using the shared word בליעל in two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר רב from Difti taught: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: Anyone who closes his eyes to צדקה is like someone who serves idols. Here it is written: 'Beware lest there be a lawless (בליעל) thought in your heart...', and there it is written: 'Lawless (בליעל) men went out.' Just as there it is about idol worship, so too here it is like idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching about how serious it is to ignore the poor. It compares refusing צדקה to עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the same word, בליעל. In the second פסוק the word describes people who lead a city to idol worship. Because of this shared word, the גמרא concludes that refusing to give to the poor is on the level of עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who closes or averts his eyes, ignores
It is written here... and it is written there (the opening of a גזירה שוה comparison)
Just as there... so too here

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that refusing צדקה is not just a missed good deed. חז"ל treat it as a very severe sin.

phrases.aramaic: וְתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּיפְתִּי,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya bar Rav from Difti taught:
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
Anyone who turns his eyes away from charity
is as if he serves idols.
It is written here:
"Beware lest there be a thought
in your heart, a lawless one, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 15:9, the same פסוק as before.

phrases.english: And it is written there:
"Lawless men went out."
phrases.notes: דברים 13:14

phrases.english: Just as there it is idol worship,
so too here it is idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּיפְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the same פסוק (דברים 15:9) to show how severe it is to ignore the poor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ignoring צדקה is like serving עבודה זרה, learned from the shared word בליעל.

steps.title: Faking need brings real need
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that whoever fakes a disability or poverty to get צדקה will end up truly suffering that condition before he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: One who pretends to be blind, or swells up his stomach, or makes himself look lame, will not leave the world until he actually becomes like that. One who takes צדקה when he does not need it will not leave the world until he actually needs it.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא was discussing swindlers, it now brings a ברייתא about their punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first gives specific examples of faking a physical problem. It then states a general rule for anyone who takes charity without needing it. The punishment matches the lie: the faked condition becomes real.
steps.whatToRemember: The fakers may give us an excuse (step 2), but they themselves are punished measure for measure: they end up truly needy.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who blinds his eye,
and one who swells up his stomach,
and one who cripples his leg,
phrases.notes: He means people who fake these problems so others will give them charity.

phrases.english: will not depart from the world
until he comes to that state.
One who takes charity and does not need it,
in the end will not depart from the world
until he comes to that state.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of swindlers by describing their punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever fakes need to take צדקה will end up truly in that condition.

steps.title: A poor person need not sell his house and belongings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic with a משנה in פאה: a poor person is not required to sell his house and household items before he may take צדקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: We do not require him to sell his house and his household items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion by quoting a משנה from מסכת פאה about who counts as poor. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה measures whether someone is poor enough for צדקה (less than 200 זוז). It says his house and the items he uses at home are not counted. He does not have to sell them first.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there (quoting a משנה from another place)
His household items, the things he uses

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in פאה (8:8) about who may take charity.

phrases.english: We do not require him

phrases.aramaic: לִמְכּוֹר אֶת בֵּיתוֹ וְאֶת כְּלֵי תַשְׁמִישׁוֹ.
phrases.english: to sell his house and his household items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic within the laws of צדקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poor person is not forced to sell his house and household items before taking צדקה.

steps.title: Challenge: must he downgrade from gold to silver to copper?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא saying that someone who used gold dishes must switch to silver, and from silver to copper. That suggests he must sell some things.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he doesn't have to sell? But a ברייתא teaches: If he used to use gold dishes, he should use silver dishes. If he used silver dishes, he should use copper dishes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the משנה can say he need not sell his belongings, when a ברייתא says he must sell his expensive dishes and use cheaper ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to protect all his household items. The ברייתא implies that he must sell expensive dishes and live on the difference before taking צדקה. The two sources look like they contradict each other. Step 7 begins the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: And not? (a challenging question: is that really so?)
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: And not?
phrases.notes: He means: is it really true that we don't make him sell anything?

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
If he was using gold dishes,
he should use silver dishes;
if silver dishes, he should use copper dishes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a poor person is not required to sell his household items.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires him to trade gold dishes for silver and silver for copper, which means selling some of his household items. That contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: רב זביד: Furniture versus eating dishes
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד answers the contradiction. The ברייתא, which requires downgrading, is about a bed and a table. The משנה, which does not require selling, is about cups and plates.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rav Zevid said: There is no difficulty. This source is talking about a bed and a table, and that source is talking about cups and plates.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד resolves the contradiction from Step 6 by saying each source is talking about different kinds of household items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said he does not have to sell his things, while the ברייתא said he must downgrade from gold to silver to copper. רב זביד splits them: furniture (bed and table) must be downgraded, but eating dishes (cups and plates) do not have to be.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the formula that opens an answer to a contradiction

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said: It is not difficult.
This one is about a bed and a table,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says he must downgrade.

phrases.english: that one is about cups and plates.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה that says he does not have to sell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (different types of items)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא seem to argue about whether a poor person must sell his belongings
steps.terutzMaskana: Furniture must be downgraded; eating dishes need not be sold

steps.title: Why are cups and plates different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why cups and plates do not need to be sold. It answers that he can say cheaper dishes disgust him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about cups and plates, that he does not have to sell them? Because he can say: Cheaper ones are disgusting to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב זביד's split and gives the answer right away: a person can be truly disgusted by eating from lower-quality dishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for keeping the fine dishes is personal disgust. Someone used to eating from gold cannot comfortably eat from cheap dishes. This reason sets up the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? A question asking for the reason behind a distinction

phrases.english: What is different about cups and plates, that he does not [have to sell them]?
Because he says: [cheaper ones] are disgusting to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב זביד's distinction
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason eating dishes do not need to be sold
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He can claim cheaper dishes disgust him

steps.title: The same argument works for furniture
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the split. With a bed and table he could also say he cannot get used to lesser ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bed and a table too: he can say, I cannot accept these lesser ones for myself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב זביד: the personal-comfort argument for dishes should also work for furniture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being used to luxury excuses him from selling his dishes, it should also excuse him from selling his bed and table, since lesser furniture is also uncomfortable for him. That would erase רב זביד's distinction and bring the contradiction back.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not accept it upon myself; it does not suit me

phrases.english: A bed and a table too:
he can say: I do not accept [lesser ones] upon myself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מטה ושולחן נמי אמר לא מקבל עילואי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason from Step 8 to attack the split in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רב זביד's distinction between furniture and dishes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The personal-comfort reason applies equally to furniture, so there is no real difference

steps.title: Only a silver luxury item must be sold
steps.stepSummary: רבא בריה דרבה explains that the ברייתא is about an unnecessary silver item, not real necessities like furniture.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא son of רבה said: [The ברייתא is talking about] a silver tool, a luxury item.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בריה דרבה accepts the challenge: furniture does not have to be sold either. He limits the ברייתא to a fancy silver extra that no one needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new line is between real necessities and pure luxuries. Necessities, even expensive ones, may be kept. A showy item that does not need to be silver at all is what the ברייתא says he must sell.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally a plow-type tool; here an example of an item that has no need to be made of silver

phrases.english: Rava son of Rabba said:
[It is talking] about a silver tool.
phrases.notes: The point is a luxury item made of silver for no real need. That kind of thing he has to sell.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא בריה דרבה במחרישה דכספא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 9 by redefining what the ברייתא is about
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא requires downgrading ordinary furniture
steps.terutzMaskana: Only unnecessary luxury items must be sold; necessities may be kept
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא בריה דרבה, a poor person keeps all his real necessities, even fancy ones. Only pointless luxuries must be sold.

steps.title: רב פפא: Before versus after collecting
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a different answer. The משנה is about before he collects צדקה, and the ברייתא is about after he has collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: There is no difficulty. Here, it is before he comes to collecting. There, it is after he comes to collecting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a whole new way to resolve the contradiction from Step 6, based on timing instead of type of item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before he takes צדקה, he does not have to sell his things in order to qualify. Once he has already collected while owning too much, he can be made to sell and downgrade to pay it back. Both sources are right, each at a different stage.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is not difficult.
Here, it is before he comes to collecting.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה: he does not have to sell anything yet.

phrases.english: There, it is after he comes to collecting.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא: now he may be made to downgrade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A separate answer to the Step 6 contradiction, instead of רב זביד's
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources argue about whether he must sell
steps.terutzMaskana: No selling is needed to start collecting; after collecting improperly he may have to sell
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not continuing רב זביד's answer. He is giving a completely different answer to the same contradiction.

steps.title: New משנה: An orphan girl's dowry
steps.stepSummary: An orphan girl married off by her mother or brothers with a small dowry can, when she grows up, claim the proper amount owed to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: An orphan girl whose mother or brothers married her off with her consent, and wrote for her one hundred or fifty זוז, can, once she grows up, take from them what is fit to be given to her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: a fatherless girl's dowry. If her family gave her too little, she can collect her proper share once she is an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though she agreed to the small amount, she was a minor then, so her agreement does not cancel her right. When she grows up she can demand the full fitting amount.

keyTerms.meaning: An orphan girl (her father has died)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
An orphan girl whose mother or brothers married her off
with her consent,

phrases.aramaic: וְכָתְבוּ לָהּ בְּמֵאָה אוֹ בַּחֲמִשִּׁים זוּז —
phrases.english: and they wrote for her one hundred or fifty zuz,
phrases.notes: This is the dowry they promised her, a small amount.

phrases.english: she can, once she grows up,
take out of their hands
what is fit to be given to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתני׳ יתומה שהשיאתה אמה או אחיה מדעתה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the צדקה discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An orphan given a small dowry may claim her proper dowry when she becomes an adult

steps.title: How to measure the proper dowry
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the second daughter gets what the father gave the first. חכמים say wealth changes, so the court appraises the estate and gives her accordingly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If he married off the first daughter, the second should be given the same way he gave the first. חכמים say: Sometimes a person is poor and becomes rich, or rich and becomes poor. Rather, they appraise the property and give her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a מחלוקת about how to figure out the fitting dowry: copy the older sister's dowry, or appraise the estate now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה uses the father's own past behavior as the measure. חכמים reject that, saying a person can go from 'poor' to 'rich' or back, so the court appraises the property instead. In steps 19-21 the גמרא shows that 'poor' and 'rich' here mean the father's spending style, not how much money he has.

keyTerms.meaning: In the same way he gave to the first daughter

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If he married off the first daughter,
it should be given to the second
in the same way that he gave to the first.
And the Rabbis say:
Sometimes a person is poor and becomes rich,
or rich and becomes poor.
Rather, they appraise the property
and give her [accordingly].

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהודה אומר אם השיא את הבת הראשונה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by arguing about how to measure what is fit to be given to her
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: match the first daughter's dowry. חכמים: appraise the current estate.
steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת is about the yardstick. רבי יהודה looks at what the father actually did before. חכמים use an appraisal of the estate, because a father's spending style can change (see steps 19-21).

steps.title: שמואל: The dowry is estimated by the father
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a daughter's dowry is set by estimating what her father would have given.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמואל said: for the dowry, we estimate based on the father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with שמואל's rule. When the court gives an orphan girl her dowry, it looks at what her father would have given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to set a dowry. One looks at the father's habits and what he would have given. The other uses a fixed share of the estate. שמואל picks the first way, and the rest of the section tests this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Support; here it means the dowry given to a daughter when she marries
We estimate based on the father, meaning what he would have given

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Shmuel said:
For the dowry, we estimate based on the father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's argument about how to set the dowry
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dowry is set by estimating what the father would have given

steps.title: A ברייתא says the court appraises the property, not the father
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says we do not guess what the father would have given. We appraise the property instead. This seems to go against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected from a ברייתא: Daughters are fed and supported from their father's property. How so? We do not say, 'If her father were alive he would have given her this much.' Rather, we appraise the property and give her. Isn't this talking about the dowry?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite of שמואל. It assumes the word 'supported' there means the dowry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly rejects guessing what the father would have given. If 'supported' means the dowry, this goes straight against שמואל. The whole challenge depends on reading 'supported' that way.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
Support for the husband, meaning the dowry

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The daughters are fed and supported
from their father's property.
How so?
We do not say: If her father were alive,
he would have given her such and such.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שָׁמִין אֶת הַנְּכָסִים וְנוֹתְנִין לַהּ.
phrases.english: Rather, we appraise the property and give her.
Is it not about support for the husband?
phrases.notes: 'Support for the husband' is the dowry, because it goes into the marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיבִי: הַבָּנוֹת נִיזּוֹנוֹת וּמִתְפַּרְנְסוֹת מִנִּכְסֵי אֲבִיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's rule
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that the dowry is estimated by the father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא rejects guessing what the father would have given. If it is about the dowry, it contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about her own support
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the ברייתא is talking about the girl's own living needs, not her dowry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: No, it is about her own support.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends שמואל. He reads 'supported' in the ברייתא as her own living costs, not the dowry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the ברייתא is about her daily support, it says nothing about the dowry. So שמואל's rule for the dowry can still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Her own support, meaning her personal living needs

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
No, it is about her own support.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לֹא, בְּפַרְנָסַת עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Supported' in the ברייתא means the dowry
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Supported' means her own needs, so the ברייתא does not deal with the dowry

steps.title: Two words must mean two kinds of support
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא uses two words, 'fed' and 'supported,' so it seems one of them must mean the dowry.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'fed and supported.' Isn't one of them the dowry and the other her own support?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן בר יצחק. If 'fed' already covers her own needs, then 'supported' should mean something else, the dowry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is built on the wording. Two separate words suggest two separate things. If so, the dowry is back in the ברייתא, and the challenge to שמואל returns.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (a leading question that sets up a challenge)

phrases.english: But it teaches 'fed and supported,'
is it not that one is support for the husband,
and one is her own support?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that the ברייתא is only about her own support
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two words mean two things, so one of them must be the dowry

steps.title: Food and clothing
steps.stepSummary: Both words mean her own support. 'Fed' is food and drink, and 'supported' is clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, both are about her own support, and it is not difficult: this one is eating and drinking, and that one is clothing and covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two words cover two parts of her personal needs: food and clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word is explained without bringing in the dowry. 'Fed' covers food and drink, and 'supported' covers clothing. So the ברייתא still says nothing against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one; both

phrases.english: No, both this and that are about her own support,
and it is not difficult:
this one is about eating and drinking,
and that one is about clothing and covering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each word is given its own meaning within her own needs
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One of the two words must mean the dowry
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Fed' means food and drink and 'supported' means clothing. Both are her own needs.

steps.title: What do 'poor' and 'rich' mean in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the משנה and asks what they mean by 'poor' and 'rich.'
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: The חכמים say: Sometimes a person is poor and becomes rich, or rich and becomes poor. Rather, we appraise the property and give her. What is 'poor' and what is 'rich'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge to שמואל. It quotes the משנה and asks for the meaning of two key words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer to this question decides whether the חכמים are talking about money or about the father's spending habits. That will matter for שמואל in the next steps.

phrases.english: We learned: And the Sages say:
Sometimes a person is poor and becomes rich,
or rich and becomes poor,
rather, we appraise the property and give her.
What is 'poor,' and what is 'rich'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new attempt to challenge שמואל, this time from the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'poor' and 'rich' in the words of the חכמים

steps.title: It cannot mean poor or rich in money
steps.stepSummary: If 'poor' and 'rich' meant actual money, then the first opinion would give a dowry the father no longer has. That makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say 'poor' means poor in property and 'rich' means rich in property, that implies the תנא קמא holds that even if the father was rich and became poor, we give her as at first. But he doesn't have it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible meaning and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים seem to be arguing against the תנא קמא. If they are pointing to money changing, then the תנא קמא would give the second daughter a big dowry even after the money is gone. Nobody can give money that does not exist, so this reading fails.

keyTerms.meaning: The first Tanna, the first opinion in the משנה
But he does not have it

phrases.english: If we say 'poor' means poor in property,
and 'rich' means rich in property,
this implies that the first Tanna holds
phrases.notes: The first Tanna here is רבי יהודה, who said the second daughter gets what the first got.

phrases.english: that even if he was rich and became poor,
we give her as much as at first;
but he doesn't have it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that 'poor' and 'rich' mean actual wealth
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the first Tanna give money the estate does not have

steps.title: Poor or rich in mindset: a refutation of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: 'Poor' and 'rich' must mean the father's spending style. Even so, the חכמים appraise the property, so they ignore the father's habits. This goes against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't 'poor' poor in mindset and 'rich' rich in mindset? And it teaches that we appraise the property and give her. So we do not follow an estimate, and this is a refutation of שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: With the money reading gone, the גמרא reads the words as spending habits. That reading turns the משנה into a strong challenge to שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say a father's spending style can change. That is why they ignore it and use a fixed appraisal of the property. That is the opposite of שמואל's 'estimate by the father,' so the גמרא calls it a תיובתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Poor in mindset; a tight-fisted spender
An estimate of a person's intentions or habits

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that 'poor' means poor in mindset,
phrases.notes: He means someone who spends like a poor man, and 'rich in mindset' is someone who spends freely.

phrases.english: and 'rich' means rich in mindset,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָתָנֵי: שָׁמִין אֶת הַנְּכָסִים וְנוֹתְנִין לָהּ,
phrases.english: and it teaches: we appraise the property and give her;
so apparently we do not go by an estimate,
and this is a refutation of Shmuel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rejection in step 20 to attack שמואל
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule of estimating by the father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים ignore the father's spending habits and use a fixed appraisal, which is the opposite of שמואל

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל is not refuted. He simply holds like רבי יהודה, who gives the second daughter what the father gave the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it according to רבי יהודה, as we learned: רבי יהודה says: If he married off the first daughter, the second is given the way he gave the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves שמואל. His rule matches the other opinion in the same משנה, the opinion of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does go by the father's habits, since he looks at what the father gave the first daughter. So the challenge only shows that שמואל disagrees with the חכמים. That is allowed, because he follows a תנא.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule, that a dowry is estimated by what the father would have given, matches רבי יהודה. The חכמים instead use a fixed appraisal of the estate.

phrases.english: He said it according to Rabbi Yehuda.
As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If he married off the first daughter,
it should be given to the second
in the way he gave to the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation in step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the אמורא to a תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל is refuted by the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי יהודה, who goes by the father's past giving

steps.title: Why not just say the הלכה follows רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's wording: if he holds like רבי יהודה, he should simply have said so.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let שמואל just say: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל gave his own rule about assessing the father instead of simply saying 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.' This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said שמואל agrees with רבי יהודה. If so, his roundabout wording seems unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what his special wording adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...

phrases.english: And let him say: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda!
phrases.notes: 'Him' is שמואל, who stated the rule about assessing the father's mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of שמואל now that step 22 has linked him to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If his view is the same as רבי יהודה's, he could have stated it more simply.

steps.title: שמואל's wording widens רבי יהודה's rule
steps.stepSummary: Saying only 'like רבי יהודה' might limit the rule to a father who already married off a daughter. שמואל's wording teaches that we always assess the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had said 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה,' I would have thought this applies only when the father married off a daughter, since he showed what he had in mind. If he did not marry one off, I would have thought we do not assess him. So שמואל teaches that רבי יהודה's reason is that we follow an assessment of the father. It makes no difference whether he married off a daughter or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל's wording teaches something extra. We assess the father's intent even if he never married off a daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה's case is a father who married off his first daughter, which shows his intent. A plain 'like רבי יהודה' could be read as limited to that case. שמואל names the reason behind it, assessment, so the rule applies in every case.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
He revealed his mind or intent
An assessment or estimate of what someone intends

phrases.english: If he had said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
I would have said: only where he married her off,
phrases.notes: 'Her' is the first daughter, whom the father married off during his lifetime.

phrases.english: since he revealed his mind.
But if he did not marry her off, no!

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: So he teaches us that the reason of Rabbi Yehuda
is that we follow the assessment,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא הִשִּׂיאָהּ וְלָא שְׁנָא לֹא הִשִּׂיאָהּ.
phrases.english: no difference whether he married her off and no difference whether he did not marry her off.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23's question about שמואל's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The wording carries an added teaching: it states the reason, which widens the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבי יהודה would apply only when the father already married off a daughter.
steps.terutzMaskana: We assess the father's intent in every case, whether or not he married off a daughter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes 'assessing the father's mind' a general rule, not a rule tied to one case.

steps.title: Why the משנה mentions 'he married her off'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions a married-off daughter to show how far the חכמים go. Even then, they refuse to assess the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the reason the משנה says 'he married her off' is to show how far the חכמים go. Even though he married her off and showed his intent, we still do not follow an assessment.
steps.whatsHappening: There is an unspoken question: if רבי יהודה's rule applies in every case, why does the משנה describe a married-off daughter? The גמרא answers that the detail is there to show the strength of the חכמים' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail does not limit רבי יהודה's rule. It shows that the חכמים reject assessment even in the strongest case, where the father clearly showed what he intended.

keyTerms.meaning: To let you know their strength (how far their view goes)

phrases.english: And that which it teaches 'he married her off,'
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's wording in the opinion of רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: is to let you know the strength of the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּהִשִּׂיאָהּ וְגַלִּי דַּעְתֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: that even though he married her off and revealed his mind,
we do not follow the assessment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Handles the problem raised by step 24: if the married-off case is not required, why does the משנה mention it?
steps.terutzResolutionType: The detail shows the strength of the other opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'he married her off' seems to limit רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase shows that the חכמים reject assessment even in the clearest case.
steps.confusionAlert: The married-off detail is not a requirement for רבי יהודה. It is there to show how firm the חכמים are.

steps.title: רב חסדא approves the ruling like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב חסדא that they teach in his name that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. רב חסדא happily agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב חסדא: We teach in your name that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. He answered: May it be God's will that you teach all fine teachings like this in my name.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא checks a ruling that was being taught in רב חסדא's name. רב חסדא confirms it warmly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms in practice that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה: we assess the father's intent. It also shows that רבא accepts this ruling, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: We teach publicly in your name

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Ḥisda:
We teach in your name: the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.
He said to him: May it be the Will
that all fine teachings such as these
you will teach in my name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא דָּרְשִׁינַן מִשְּׁמָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical ruling confirming רבי יהודה's view, which שמואל follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: we assess the father's intent for the second daughter's dowry.

steps.title: רבא also rules like רבי's fixed tenth
steps.stepSummary: רבא elsewhere rules like רבי, who gives an orphan daughter a fixed tenth of the estate. That seems to ignore any assessment of the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבא really say this? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי says: a daughter who is supported by her brothers takes a tenth of the estate. And רבא said: the הלכה follows רבי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's ruling like רבי יהודה. He also ruled like רבי, who sets a fixed amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי gives a set tenth of the estate, with no estimate of what the father wanted. Following רבי seems to rule out following רבי יהודה's assessment approach, so רבא seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is supported from the brothers' inheritance

phrases.english: And did Rava say this?
But isn't it taught: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' here means רבי יהודה הנשיא, not רבי יהודה from the משנה.

phrases.english: A daughter who is sustained from the brothers
takes one-tenth of the property.
And Rava said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's report in step 26 using another ruling of his.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A fixed tenth (רבי) seems to rule out assessing the father's intent (רבי יהודה), yet רבא follows both.

steps.title: Assess when possible, otherwise a tenth
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. When we can assess the father's intent, we follow it. When we cannot, the daughter gets a tenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. Here, we assessed him. There, we did not assess him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves רבא's two rulings by splitting the cases. Each ruling applies to a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father's intent can be estimated, רבי יהודה's assessment decides the dowry. If it cannot be estimated, we fall back on רבי's fixed tenth. The two rulings work together instead of clashing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (there is no contradiction)

steps.whatToRemember: The dowry follows our assessment of the father's intent (רבי יהודה, שמואל, רבא). Only when his intent cannot be assessed does the daughter get a fixed tenth of the estate (רבי).

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where we assessed him,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the ruling like רבי יהודה. 'That' in the next line is the ruling like רבי.

phrases.english: that is where we did not assess him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא דַּאֲמֵידְנֵיהּ הָא דְּלָא אֲמֵידְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27's contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ruling applies to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's two rulings contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Assessment applies when the father's intent is known. The fixed tenth applies when it is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical order for a dowry: first try to estimate the father's intent, and only if that is impossible give a tenth.

steps.title: Two reports of רבי's ruling prove the assessment distinction
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה reports that רבי once gave a daughter one-twelfth, not one-tenth. The two reports clash unless one case involved assessing the father and the other did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is logical too. רב אדא בר אהבה reported that רבי once gave a daughter one-twelfth of the estate. That clashes with the rule of one-tenth. So it must be that the twelfth was given when they could assess the father, and the tenth applies when they could not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to support the answer from step 28. It shows that רבי himself sometimes gave a different amount than a tenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי always gave a fixed tenth, why did he once give a twelfth? The best explanation is that in that story they knew what the father wanted, so they followed it. The tenth is only the default when the father's wishes are unknown.

keyTerms.meaning: So too, it is logical. This introduces support for what was just said.
We assessed him, meaning we could tell what the father intended

phrases.english: So too, it is reasonable,
as Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
There was an incident, and Rabbi gave her
phrases.notes: "Her" is an orphan daughter who needed a dowry from her father's estate.

phrases.english: one-twelfth of the property!
These contradict each other.
Rather, isn't it correct to learn from this:
this one is where we assessed him,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the twelfth. They knew what the father wanted and followed it.

phrases.english: that one is where we did not assess him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 28 with a reported incident
steps.raayaObject: The distinction that the tenth applies only when the father cannot be assessed
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אדא בר אהבה's report that רבי once gave one-twelfth

steps.title: The proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof. Assessing the father decides the amount when possible, and the tenth is only the fallback.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this section by agreeing that the proof works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the contradiction from step 27. Following רבי (a tenth) and following רבי יהודה (assess the father) fit together, because each applies in a different situation.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. The proof is accepted.

steps.whatToRemember: If we can tell what the father wanted, we follow it. If not, the daughter gets a tenth of the estate.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 29
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Assessment of the father comes first. A tenth is the default only when he cannot be assessed.

steps.title: רבי's rule: a daughter takes a tenth of the estate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to discuss רבי's rule itself. An orphan daughter supported by her brothers takes a tenth of the estate for her dowry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the rule itself. רבי said: a daughter who is supported from her brothers' inheritance takes a tenth of the estate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to the rule of רבי that was mentioned earlier, so it can examine it more closely. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the rule was only mentioned in passing. Now the גמרא quotes it in full, so it can raise a challenge against it.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. The גמרא returns to a statement quoted earlier.
Who is supported, meaning she gets her food and needs paid for

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabbi said:
A daughter who is supported from the brothers
takes a tenth of the property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the rule of רבי cited in step 27 to discuss it directly
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An orphan daughter takes a tenth of the estate for her dowry.

steps.title: With ten daughters, the son gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: Others challenge רבי. If each daughter takes a tenth, ten daughters would take the whole estate, and the son would be left with nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי: by your rule, a man with ten daughters and one son leaves the son nothing, because the daughters take it all.
steps.whatsHappening: Unnamed questioners attack רבי's rule by showing that it leads to an impossible result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten tenths add up to the whole estate. But the son is the one who actually inherits by Torah law, so a rule that leaves him empty-handed cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: According to your words or opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Daughters do not inherit when there is a son. The tenth is a dowry taken from the son's inheritance. That is why the son ending up with nothing is such a problem.

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi: According to your words,

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עֶשֶׂר בָּנוֹת וּבֵן,
phrases.english: one who has ten daughters and a son,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ לַבֵּן בִּמְקוֹם בָּנוֹת כְּלוּם!
phrases.english: the son has nothing where there are daughters!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's rule from step 31
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's rule that each daughter takes a tenth of the estate
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ten daughters taking a tenth each would use up the entire estate and leave the son, the real heir, with nothing.

steps.title: Each daughter takes a tenth of what is left, then they even out
steps.stepSummary: רבי explains that each daughter takes a tenth of what remains after the one before her. Afterward, all the daughters share their dowries equally, and the son still keeps a portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: this is what I mean. The first daughter takes a tenth of the estate. The second takes a tenth of what the first left, and the third takes a tenth of what the second left. Then they put it together and split it equally.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers the challenge by explaining how the tenth is actually calculated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tenth is not taken from the original estate each time. It is taken from whatever remains, so each share gets smaller and something is always left for the son. Because later daughters would otherwise get less, the daughters redistribute their shares so that all of them get the same amount.

keyTerms.meaning: They go back and divide again

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's tenth is a tenth of whatever remains, so the son is never wiped out. Afterward the daughters even out their shares.

phrases.english: He said to them: This is what I say:
The first takes a tenth of the property,
the second, a tenth from what the first left,
and the third, a tenth from what the second left.
And then they go back and divide equally.
phrases.notes: The daughters pool their dowries and split them evenly, so the first one doesn't end up with more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies how the rule is applied: a tenth of the remainder, not of the original estate
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each daughter takes a tenth of the original estate, so ten daughters would take everything.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each daughter takes a tenth of what remains, and then the daughters redistribute equally, so the son keeps a share.
